'''John Matthew Sullivan''' (born February 25, 1963) is an American mathematician who works in Germany as a professor at [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. His research includes work on [[knot theory]], [[constant-mean-curvature surface]]s, [[Weaire–Phelan structure|mathematical foams]], [[scientific visualization]], and [[mesh generation]].<ref name="cv">[https://page.math.tu-berlin.de/~sullivan/vita2-14.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Sullivan was born in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], and graduated [[summa cum laude]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1985. He earned a master's degree from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1986, and a doctorate from [[Princeton University]] in 1990 under the supervision of [[Frederick J. Almgren, Jr.]]<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=17385}}</ref>

==Career==
After postdoctoral studies at [[The Geometry Center]] and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], Sullivan joined the faculty of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1997. He moved to Berlin in 2003, and chaired the [[Berlin Mathematical School]] from 2012 to 2014.<ref name="cv"/>

==Awards==
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society|Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref>
